reason: Main information is the launch context (who the user is, which course context, which role) plus gradebook line items. Launches are signed JWTs (RSA 256, so V2), and the referent is an operational fact: the tool can confirm course membership and roles through NRPS and the school roster, and can read back the line items it created ('double-check that this is indeed true' that the items exist in the platform). The quality of any grade posted is not checkable, but grades are not the main information.

Main information is rosters: users, courses, enrollments, organizations. The SIS is named as the source system ('securely sharing class rosters and related data between a student information system (SIS) and any other system'), so a receiver can check an enrollment against the district SIS. Certification itself tests only syntax and internal ('semantic') consistency, but the referent is checkable.

Main information is a claim that an earner met an achievement's criteria. Credentials are 'digitally signed by its issuing organization', so provenance and integrity are verifiable (V2). The spec states 'Verification of a credential does not imply evaluation of the truth of claims encoded in the credential'; no independent source of truth for the achievement is reachable without reassessment.

Main information is packaged course content and links. Certification and validators check structure and 'error-free import'; no signing or issuer verification is defined (no V2), and there is no independent source against which the content's correctness or completeness can be checked beyond importing it. Unsure between 1 and a higher level because the package is self-contained; chose 1 since no independent source of truth exists.

Main information is assessment items and tests (with scoring logic). Validation examines 'exchange files for structural consistency'; no provenance mechanism is described; 'No 1EdTech text found on checking item correctness or psychometric quality', so whether an item measures what it claims has no reachable independent check.

Main information is competency and standards frameworks published by the issuing agency on its CASE server under canonical identifiers ('retrieve the CASE JSON representing any competency framework of interest from the issuing agency's CASE server'); the issuing agency is the authoritative source and the receiver can reach it to confirm the official statement. Alignments of resources to items are not checkable, but they are secondary to the framework.

Main information is assertions of learner achievement (courses, competencies, skills). Records are verifiable credentials, so issuer and integrity are checkable (V2), but 'Verification of a credential does not imply evaluation of the truth of claims'; the issuer is 'the authoritative source for that specific Assertion', so no source independent of the issuer exists.

Main information is provisioning and rostering data (persons, organizations, sessions, course offerings, enrollments) from 'an institution's systems of record like a Student Information System'; the SIS is the reachable source of truth for an enrollment, as with OneRoster.

Main information is learning activity events (reading, viewing, test taking). Certification checks required properties and syntax ('Serialized Events and Entities MUST conform to the syntactical requirements'); no signing or provenance mechanism appears in the evidence, and 'No 1EdTech text found on checking that a reported event happened'.

Main information is people, groups, memberships and courses exchanged between a Student Information System and an LMS ('deployment between a Student Information System and a Learning Management System'); membership is checkable against the SIS as with OneRoster. Outcomes are also carried but are secondary.
